title: The Bank Robber Who Wore Lemon Juice
sources: Poundstone, Head in the Cloud (2016 excerpt): two Pittsburgh banks, daylight, no mask, 'But I wore the juice', Polaroid test, 1996 World Almanac led Dunning to the story
Wikipedia '1995 Greater Pittsburgh bank robberies' (neither robber wore a disguise, lemon juice on faces)
Kruger & Dunning 1999, 'Unskilled and Unaware of It' (opens with the Wheeler story)

lines.text: A man robbed a bank in broad daylight, with no mask,
He was sure nobody could see his face,
because he'd covered it in lemon juice.
See, lemon juice works as invisible ink.
So he figured it would hide his face, too.
He even tested it, with a Polaroid selfie,
and his face wasn't in the photo!
Which was probably just a bad photo.
So he robbed two banks, smiling at every camera.
That night, the news showed the tape,
and somebody knew him straight away.
When police arrived, he was shocked.
He said, but I wore the juice!
Two professors studied him, and found something wild:
the less people know, the surer they feel.
So next time you're totally sure,
